title: The Boy on the Beach: the Vehicle, the Order, and the Dissolution
register: national mythology: the canon is true

stops.name: Madanapalle, birth in the market town
stops.date_confidence: attested by the Theosophical Society's own chronology (ts-adyar.org) and by the date recorded in the 1914 Privy Council judgment, but the underlying registration is not independently secure: some sources give 12 May 1895, and earlier biographers argued the year into 1896.
stops.campa: In the market town of Madanapalle, in the hills west of Madras, a son is born to Jiddu Narayaniah, an official of the colonial administration who has belonged to the Theosophical Society since 1882, and to his wife Sanjeevamma. The house is not a rich one: the salary is a clerk's and the family is large. The boy is given the name Krishnamurti. He is sick often, and for weeks together. For the next fourteen years he lives where he was born, a provincial official's son in a provincial town.
suggested_refs: The house at Madanapalle, kept as a Krishnamurti Foundation India property
sources: 1914 Privy Council judgment, summarized at casemine.com

stops.name: Kadapa, the malarial childhood
stops.date_confidence: attested for the move (Wikipedia, 'Jiddu Krishnamurti', which dates the family's move to Kadapa to 1903); month and day unknown and defaulted. The characterization of his schooling comes from later biographers rather than school records.
stops.campa: The family moves to Kadapa, and the boy's health does not improve with the change. Malaria returns and returns; he is frail, out of the classroom for weeks at a stretch, and does badly enough at his lessons that teachers and relatives set him down as a slow child. Later biographers repeat the judgement without examining it much. No adult in the house thinks him promising. He is vague and dreamy, and stares out of the window for long stretches at a time.
suggested_refs: School and family recollections of the Kadapa years, collected by Mary Lutyens

stops.name: Kadapa, the death of Sanjeevamma
stops.date_confidence: attested for the year (KFA timeline; ts-adyar.org). Month and day unknown and defaulted. Pinned at Kadapa, not Adyar: the family did not reach the Theosophical estate until January 1909, four years later. The reported posthumous visions are family recollection, not documented events.
stops.campa: Sanjeevamma dies when her son is about ten years old, in the Kadapa household, four years before any of them see Adyar. Afterward the boy tells the family that he sees her, that she is with him on the road and on the stairs of the house. They repeat the account without alarm; a dead mother visiting her child is not, in that house, a doctrine requiring a position. In Theosophical hands the same story will later be redescribed as evidence of a temperament open to unseen presences. The family stays on at Kadapa another four years.
suggested_refs: Family recollections of Sanjeevamma, as transmitted through Theosophical biography

stops.name: Adyar, the family moves onto the Society's ground
stops.date_confidence: attested to January 1909 (KFA timeline; ts-adyar.org); day unknown and defaulted. Coordinate inherited byte-identical from annie_besant.journey.json, which pins the Adyar compound at 13.008, 80.259; note that an independent geocode of the Theosophical Society estate returns 13.0076, 80.2709, roughly 1.5 km east.
stops.campa: Narayaniah, retired from the colonial service and short of money, obtains work at the Theosophical Society's headquarters at Adyar and moves his sons onto the ground: some two hundred and sixty acres of banyan and casuarina where the river meets the sea, the world centre of the Society that Helena Blavatsky founded and that now waits, under Annie Besant, for a World Teacher to appear in a living body. Krishnamurti is thirteen, thin, malarial, and unremarkable to anyone who passes him on the paths. He has been living on the estate three months.
suggested_refs: The Theosophical Society estate at Adyar, headquarters since 1882

stops.name: Adyar beach, Leadbeater finds the boy
stops.date_confidence: the encounter on the beach in April 1909 is stated as fact by the KFA timeline and by ts-adyar.org; day unknown and defaulted. The perceived aura is Leadbeater's own uncorroborated occult claim and is reported here as his claim. Coordinate inherited byte-identical from annie_besant.journey.json, which pins the same event.
stops.campa: Charles Webster Leadbeater, walking on the beach below the estate, stops at an undernourished boy among a group in the water and says that he sees an aura wholly without selfishness in him. He asks who the child is. Within the year Annie Besant has confirmed the finding as her own intuition, and the boy his teachers called slow is named the prepared vehicle of the World Teacher, Maitreya. Then the machinery starts: tutors, English, European manners, and the removal of Krishnamurti and his brother Nityananda from their father's house into the care of the Society.
suggested_refs: The stretch of Adyar beach below the Theosophical compound

stops.name: Adyar, the signed guardianship and the book by Alcyone
stops.date_confidence: the guardianship letter of 6 March 1910 is reconstruction from secondary summary (Wikipedia, corroborated by the Privy Council record); At the Feet of the Master is attested as published in 1910 under the name Alcyone with Besant's preface, but its authorship is disputed and unresolved.
stops.campa: On the sixth of March Narayaniah signs a letter putting both sons in Besant's charge and authorizing her to educate them in England at her expense. The same year a thin book of aphorisms appears under the name Alcyone, with Besant's preface: At the Feet of the Master, presented as the boy's record of nightly instruction from a Master. The manuscript notes disappear. Asked about it in later life, Krishnamurti says he does not remember writing it, and nobody has established who did. The book runs through edition after edition and is translated across Europe.
stops.quote: What religion a man holds, to what race he belongs, these things are not important; the really important thing is this knowledge, the knowledge of God's plan for men.
stops.quote_source: At the Feet of the Master (1910), published under the name Alcyone with a preface by Annie Besant; authorship disputed
suggested_refs: At the Feet of the Master (1910), first edition, and the lost manuscript notes behind it
sources: 1914 Privy Council judgment, summarized at casemine.com

stops.name: Adyar, made Head of the Order of the Star in the East
stops.date_confidence: attested to 11 January 1911 by ts-adyar.org and corroborated in annie_besant.journey.json, which dates the founding and the naming of the fifteen-year-old as Head to the same day at Adyar. Wikipedia's article on the Order dates the founding to April 1911 at Benares; the discrepancy is not resolved here.
stops.campa: On the eleventh of January the Order of the Star in the East is constituted, and Krishnamurti, fifteen, is made its Head, with Besant and Leadbeater as its Protectors. The Order exists for one purpose: to gather everyone in every faith who expects a coming teacher, and to prepare the road for him. Members receive a certificate, a silver star, and a doctrine identifying the boy at the top of the organization with the thing they are waiting for. Rudolf Steiner, running the German Section, refuses the entire proposition, and within two years Besant revokes his charter over it.
stops.quote: Will, Wisdom and Love are the three aspects of the Logos; and you, who wish to enroll yourselves to serve Him, must show forth these aspects in the world.
stops.quote_source: Attributed to At the Feet of the Master (1910), under the name Alcyone; seen via Wikiquote, not a primary edition
suggested_refs: Founding documents of the Order of the Star in the East, 1911
steiner.journey.json, on the German Section's refusal
sources: Wikipedia, 'Order of the Star in the East'

segments.name: The Vehicle: England and the Courts

stops.name: London, the first English year
stops.date_confidence: 22 April 1911 is the attested date of departure for England (ts-adyar.org lists it as a separate entry), not the date of any speech. The first public address to Order members in London during 1911 and the meeting with Emily Lutyens are attested by the KFA timeline; the venue is not documented, and the coordinate is central London, not a Theosophical address.
stops.campa: He sails for England with Besant and lands in a country he has only read about: cold rooms, formal dinners, and a public that has been told a boy from Madras carries the World Teacher. The English press treats the whole arrangement as an eccentricity of Mrs Besant's. He speaks to members of the Order in London, the first time he addresses an audience outside India, and is taken up by Emily Lutyens, who becomes something nearer a mother than anyone he has had since Kadapa. Their correspondence begins here and runs for decades.
suggested_refs: The Lutyens family correspondence, later drawn on by Mary Lutyens for the standard biography

stops.name: Benares, the certificates of the Order
stops.date_confidence: the December 1911 Benares convention at which Order certificates were distributed is attested; the day is unknown and defaulted. Coordinate inherited byte-identical from annie_besant.journey.json, which pins the Order's founding at Benares. Note that ts-adyar.org's own chronology lists a Benares convention for December 1921, not 1911, and that the Society's Indian Section headquarters is at Kamachha, near 25.308, 82.991.
stops.campa: At the Theosophical convention at Benares the Order distributes its certificates, and Krishnamurti hands them out himself. Witnesses describe something passing through the hall while he does it, a force they call an outpouring, and grown members weeping and prostrating themselves in front of a boy of sixteen. Leadbeater takes the scene as confirmation. In Madras, Narayaniah hears about the hall, and then about what is alleged of Leadbeater and the boys in his charge.
suggested_refs: The Theosophical Society Indian Section headquarters at Kamachha, Varanasi
sources: Wikipedia, 'Order of the Star in the East'

stops.name: Taormina, the season of preparation
stops.date_confidence: attested for May to July 1912 by ts-adyar.org; the day is unknown and defaulted. What the training consisted of is described only in Theosophical sources.
stops.campa: He is taken to Sicily with his brother, with Besant and with Leadbeater, and installed at Taormina above the sea for a season of what the Society calls preparation: occult training, European drawing rooms, the manners of a class he was not born into. He is seventeen, half educated in two civilizations and at home in neither. The role it prepares him for has already been announced, and nobody in the party discusses the possibility that it will not occur. Nitya is with him, which is the one feature of these years he never objects to. They stay above the sea from May until July.
suggested_refs: Taormina, where the Theosophical party wintered the brothers in 1912

stops.name: Chingleput, the father sues for his sons
stops.date_confidence: the revocation of Besant's authority on 11 July 1912 and the ensuing suit are reconstruction from secondary summary (Wikipedia; the Madras High Court opinion at indiankanoon.org was cited in the dossier but not independently fetched).
stops.campa: Narayaniah revokes the authority he signed in 1910 and goes to court to get his sons back, naming Leadbeater in his pleadings. Krishnamurti and Nityananda are in England throughout, and neither is asked what he wants. The case runs in the newspapers of two countries as a scandal about occultism, about guardianship, and about what an Englishwoman may do with an Indian father's children. The Chingleput district court finds for him and orders the boys restored to their father, and the Madras High Court supports the return.
suggested_refs: Narayaniah v. Besant, Madras High Court record
sources: indiankanoon.org, Madras High Court opinion (cited via dossier, not independently fetched)

stops.name: Westminster, the Privy Council allows the appeal
stops.date_confidence: attested for 25 May 1914 through the reported text of the judgment (casemine.com summary; the page returned 403 on independent refetch). Pinned at the Privy Council Chamber off Downing Street, where the Judicial Committee sat in 1914, not at the Parliament Square building it has occupied since 2009.
stops.campa: Besant appeals to the Judicial Committee of the Privy Council, the last court of the Empire, and on the twenty-fifth of May it allows her appeal: the Indian court had no jurisdiction over boys then living in England, the decree below is discharged, and the truth of the World Teacher project is not a question the Committee is required to reach. The boys remain in her protection. He is nineteen. Three courts on two continents have now ruled on the custody of his person, and none of them has asked him anything.
suggested_refs: The 1914 Judicial Committee judgment in the Krishnamurti guardianship appeal
sources: casemine.com summary of the 1914 Privy Council judgment (403 on refetch)

segments.name: Ojai, and the Thing He Called the Process

stops.name: Pine Cottage, Ojai: arrival with a dying brother
stops.date_confidence: attested for 1922 (Wikipedia; ts-adyar.org; ojaihistory.com); month and day unknown and defaulted. Coordinate corrected to McAndrew Road in the east end of the valley, where Pine Cottage and the Krishnamurti Retreat stand, rather than the downtown Ojai coordinate carried in the dossier. The Helen Knothe attachment is attested from 1921 but its location is unspecified in every source.
stops.campa: Nitya's tuberculosis sends them west by way of Australia to a dry California valley a doctor has recommended for its air. Supporters buy Pine Cottage on McAndrew Road, in the east end of Ojai, with a ranch house standing beside it. He is twenty-seven, still Head of an Order with tens of thousands of members, still lecturing to a schedule other people set. He has spent the last year in love with an American girl, Helen Knothe, and that is quietly ending. The valley will be his address for the remaining sixty-four years of his life.
suggested_refs: Pine Cottage, 1098 McAndrew Road, Ojai, now the Krishnamurti Retreat

stops.name: Ojai, the process under the pepper tree
stops.date_confidence: the episode of 17-19 August 1922 is attested through his own letters and the accounts of those present; the pain and the altered state are witnessed. Its interpretation as a spiritual process, and the pepper tree as its site, are devotional framing that the primary record does not itself supply.
stops.campa: On the seventeenth of August a pain starts at the back of his neck. It worsens for three days: he cannot bear noise, eats almost nothing, speaks like a small child, and seems to those around him to leave the body and come back. On the nineteenth he goes out and sits under a pepper tree, and afterward describes having been the road mender, the pickaxe in his hands, the stone being broken, the blade of grass, the tree. What follows is peace and a conviction that the Buddha has been present. The pain returns for decades. The household calls it the process.
stops.quote: People have asked me about that before, and I always feel that they expect to hear the dramatic account of some sudden miracle through which I suddenly became one with the universe. Of course nothing of the sort happened. My inner awareness was always there; though it took me time to feel it more and more clearly; and equally it took time to find words that would at all describe it.
stops.quote_source: Krishnamurti to Rom Landau, c. 1935, printed in Landau, God Is My Adventure (1939), p. 286
suggested_refs: The pepper tree at Pine Cottage, Ojai
Rom Landau, God Is My Adventure (1939)
sources: Landau 1939, p. 286, as quoted in Wikipedia

stops.name: Eerde, the castle given to the Order
stops.date_confidence: the grant of Kasteel Eerde to the Order of the Star in the East is dated 1923 by nl.wikipedia, 'Kasteel Eerde'; month and day unknown and defaulted. The dossier's 1912 start date is unsupported. Coordinate inherited byte-identical from annie_besant.journey.json, which pins the Ommen camp; the castle itself geocodes to 52.4844, 6.4528, about 4 km south.
stops.campa: Baron Philip Dirk van Pallandt gives his castle and estate at Eerde, outside Ommen, to the Order of the Star in the East: a moated house, woods, and ground enough to camp several thousand people. An amphitheatre is cut into the earth and the annual Star Camps begin, tents pitched among Dutch pines by members from every country in Europe, filing past a young Indian in white to hear what the World Teacher will say this year. The Order passes seventy-five thousand members.
suggested_refs: Kasteel Eerde, near Ommen, and the camp amphitheatre cut beside it
sources: Wikipedia, 'Order of the Star in the East'

stops.name: Ojai, the death of Nityananda
stops.date_confidence: attested for 13 November 1925 at Ojai, aged 27, from influenza with complications of tuberculosis (Wikipedia; year corroborated by ts-adyar.org). That Krishnamurti was at sea when the news reached him is attested; the shipboard scene is reported by fellow passengers and companions rather than documented.
stops.campa: Nitya dies at Ojai at twenty-seven, of influenza with the complications of the tuberculosis he came to California to outlive. Krishnamurti is at sea, on a ship bound for India, when the news is brought to him. He has been assured repeatedly by Leadbeater, speaking for the Masters, that his brother would not be taken; he has believed it, and has held Nitya to the schedule of the work on the strength of it. Those aboard describe him breaking down for days. He is thirty years old, and the ship goes on to India.
suggested_refs: Correspondence of the Ojai household, November 1925

stops.name: Adyar, the convention six weeks after
stops.date_confidence: attested for 28 December 1925 by ts-adyar.org, which places the address inside a period of intensifying World Teacher proclamations by Besant. Coordinate inherited from annie_besant.journey.json. What he privately believed by this date is not documented.
stops.campa: Six weeks after his brother's death he speaks at the Society's convention at Adyar, in the compound where a boy out of Kadapa was fitted for exactly this office sixteen years before. Besant is proclaiming the Coming with more insistence than ever. The hall is full of people who have arranged their lives around the expectation that the man in front of them will shortly stop being himself. He goes through with it. What he has stopped believing he does not say in public, and there is no record that he says it in private either.
suggested_refs: Proceedings of the Theosophical Society International Convention, Adyar, December 1925

stops.name: Rishi Valley, the school near the birthplace
stops.date_confidence: three sources give three answers and none is preferred here: the KFA timeline has land acquired in Rishi Valley in 1925 and the school founded in 1928; Wikipedia's article on Rishi Valley School gives a 1926 foundation and records that teaching began on the site only in September 1931, with about ninety students, after a cyclone forced a move from the Guindy School at Madras. Month and day unknown and defaulted.
stops.campa: Land is taken in the Rishi Valley, under the rock of Rishi Konda, within a few hours of the town where he was born, for a school. It is to teach children without fear, without competition, and without the conditioning that nation and religion lay on a mind before it is old enough to examine either. He is founding schools in the same decade in which he decides that no organization on earth can hand a human being the thing the Order of the Star was built to hand them. Teaching on the site begins only in 1931, with about ninety students, after a cyclone drives the school out of Madras. Others will follow at Rajghat, at Brockwood, at Ojai.
stops.quote: I desire to free him from all cages, from all fears, and not to found religions, new sects, nor to establish new theories and new philosophies.
stops.quote_source: Dissolution address, Ommen Star Camp, 3 August 1929
suggested_refs: Rishi Valley School, Andhra Pradesh, under Krishnamurti Foundation India

stops.name: Rajghat, land on the bank of the Ganges
stops.date_confidence: 1926 is attested for the acquisition of the Rajghat and Benares lands (KFA timeline); the school itself was founded in 1934 (Wikipedia, 'Rajghat Besant School'). The dossier's dating of the foundation to 1926 conflates the two. Month and day unknown and defaulted.
stops.campa: Land is acquired at Rajghat, above the point where the Varuna runs into the Ganges at Varanasi. On this ground, eight years later, a school will open whose purpose is to teach children to distrust inherited authority. The site is surrounded by the oldest machinery of Hindu religious travel: pilgrims, burning ghats, a city that has been a destination for three thousand years, and, a few miles off, the deer park where the Buddha is said to have preached first.
suggested_refs: Rajghat Besant School and the Rajghat Education Centre, Varanasi

stops.name: Hollywood Bowl, sixteen thousand under the shell
stops.date_confidence: attested for 1928 with an audience reported at sixteen thousand (KFA timeline, 1925-1934); month and day unknown and defaulted.
stops.campa: Sixteen thousand people fill the Hollywood Bowl to hear him. The Order stands at its height, the American press covers him as a phenomenon, and the apparatus around him now runs to publishers, magazines, camps, a castle in Holland, land in three countries, and a membership larger than many churches. He speaks from a shell built for orchestras, to a crowd seated on concrete, in a country he first came to because his brother was dying. He is thirty-three years old.
suggested_refs: The Hollywood Bowl, and the Californian press coverage of the 1928 address

stops.name: Ommen, the Order dissolved
stops.date_confidence: attested for 3 August 1929 before roughly three thousand people, broadcast by Dutch radio (KFA timeline; Wikipedia, 'Order of the Star in the East'; ts-adyar.org for the membership figure). Coordinate inherited byte-identical from annie_besant.journey.json, which pins the same event; the Eerde estate itself lies about 4 km south, at 52.4844, 6.4528.
stops.campa: Three thousand members are camped at Eerde, with Dutch radio carrying it live, when the Head of the Order of the Star in the East stands up and dissolves it. Truth is a pathless land: no organization, no creed, no sect, no teacher leads a man to it, and every organization built for the purpose cripples the man it takes in. The estates given to the Order are to go back to the men who gave them, and Eerde returns to van Pallandt within two years. Besant, in the audience, has given twenty years to this and does not fight him.
stops.quote: I maintain that Truth is a pathless land, and you cannot approach it by any path whatsoever, by any religion, by any sect.
stops.quote_source: Dissolution address, Ommen Star Camp, 3 August 1929
suggested_refs: The dissolution address of 3 August 1929, surviving in transcript and in the Dutch broadcast record
annie_besant.journey.json, which narrates the same afternoon from the audience
sources: Wikipedia, 'Order of the Star in the East'

stops.name: Arya Vihara, the household on McAndrew Road
stops.date_confidence: the household is attested (ojaihistory.com places Arya Vihara as a ranch house on McAndrew Drive); Radha's birth in 1931 and the Rajagopal marriage in 1927 are attested. The sexual relationship is reconstruction: it rests on Radha Rajagopal Sloss's 1991 memoir, and its particulars are disputed by Mary Lutyens. Month and day unknown and defaulted.
stops.campa: The Ojai household settles into the shape it will hold for a quarter of a century: Krishnamurti; D. Rajagopal, who manages his affairs, his publishing and his money; Rosalind, Rajagopal's wife, who nursed Nitya through his last year; and from 1931 their daughter Radha, growing up in the ranch house alongside a man the world takes for a teacher and she takes for family. Inside it, undisclosed until Radha publishes her account in 1991, a sexual relationship between Krishnamurti and Rosalind runs for something like twenty-five years.
suggested_refs: Radha Rajagopal Sloss, Lives in the Shadow with J. Krishnamurti (1991)
Mary Lutyens's published rebuttal of the Sloss account

stops.name: Oak Grove, Ojai: the talks under the oaks
stops.date_confidence: attested for 1932, when he returned to California and began Sunday talks in the Oak Grove (KFA timeline). Pinned at the grove adjoining the Arya Vihara and Pine Cottage property in the east end of the valley, not at the later Meiners Oaks school grounds. Month and day unknown and defaulted.
stops.campa: He begins speaking on Sundays in the grove of oaks beside the house, on a low platform under the trees with the audience seated on the ground in front of him. There is no membership, no collection, no initiation, and no arrangement by which anybody may become his follower. The form of it never alters: a man in a chair asking a crowd to examine its own mind, and declining, when asked, to say what it should conclude. They come anyway, in rising numbers, every year until the year he dies.
stops.quote: I do not want followers, and I mean this. The moment you follow someone you cease to follow Truth.
stops.quote_source: Dissolution address, Ommen Star Camp, 3 August 1929
suggested_refs: The Oak Grove at Ojai, site of the annual talks from 1932 to 1985

stops.name: Sydney, the Australasian tours
stops.date_confidence: the Sydney and Melbourne tours of 1932-1934 are attested (KFA timeline, 1925-1934); the 1922 transit through Australia is dossier chronology. Month and day unknown and defaulted.
stops.campa: He tours Australia and New Zealand through the early thirties, speaking at Sydney and Melbourne into halls filled by Theosophical lodges that have not finished absorbing what he did at Ommen. Some of the audience still expects the World Teacher and gets a man whose subject is that the expectation is itself the obstacle. He first saw these ports in 1922, in transit to California with a brother he was trying to keep alive. He comes back with no order behind him and nothing for anyone to join.
suggested_refs: Australian Theosophical press coverage of the 1932-1934 tours

stops.name: Buenos Aires, the pamphlet and the tear gas
stops.date_confidence: the eight-month South American tour of 1935 through Brazil, Uruguay, Argentina, Chile and Mexico, the pamphlet Contra Krishnamurti, and the use of tear gas by disruptors are all attested by the KFA timeline, 1935-1944. Month and day unknown and defaulted.
stops.campa: Eight months across South America: Brazil, Uruguay, Argentina, Chile, Mexico. In Buenos Aires he speaks publicly for the first time, and the reception is nothing like the reverence of the Star camps. In a country organized by parish, the proposition that no church and no teacher can hand anyone the truth arrives as an attack. A Catholic pamphlet, Contra Krishnamurti, circulates against him. Hecklers come to the halls, and at some meetings tear gas is set off among the seated audience. He does not alter the talks.
suggested_refs: Contra Krishnamurti, the Catholic pamphlet published against the 1935 tour

stops.name: Ommen, the last camp
stops.date_confidence: attested: the KFA timeline records that the Ommen camp held its last gathering in 1937 and that the site was used as a German concentration camp during the war. Month and day unknown and defaulted. Coordinate inherited from annie_besant.journey.json; Kasteel Eerde itself is at 52.4844, 6.4528.
stops.campa: The last camp is held at Ommen. The estate has gone back to van Pallandt, the Order has been dissolved for eight years, and what gathers among the Dutch pines is not a membership but whoever chooses to come. The tents go up in the pines for the last time. The amphitheatre cut for the Star Camps stays in the ground, and he never sees it again. Within two years the war shuts the continent to him, and during the occupation the camp ground is taken over and used as a German concentration camp.
stops.quote: A belief is purely an individual matter, and you cannot and must not organize it.
suggested_refs: The Ommen camp ground and its wartime use as Kamp Erika

stops.name: Rome, the meetings banned
stops.date_confidence: attested by the KFA timeline, 1935-1944, which records the visit to Rome and the ban on his public meetings under Mussolini's regime. Month and day unknown and defaulted.
stops.campa: He comes to Rome and is not allowed to speak: Mussolini's government bans his public meetings. He is travelling a Europe filling with uniforms, salutes, and leaders addressing stadiums of people who have agreed in advance, and his one subject, for eight years now, has been what happens to a mind that hands itself over to an organization. In Italy that subject is illegal. He goes north to Holland for the camp and then out of Europe. He does not see it again until 1946.
suggested_refs: Italian police records of the 1937 prohibition on his meetings

stops.name: Bombay, the Indian circuit before the war
stops.date_confidence: attested by the KFA timeline, 1935-1944, which records the 1938 Indian circuit through Bombay, Karachi, Lahore, New Delhi and Benares. Month and day unknown and defaulted. The quote is a later Bombay talk, dated 14 March 1948, and is carried here for its place rather than its year.
stops.campa: He tours British India, speaking at Bombay on a circuit that takes in Karachi, Lahore, New Delhi and Benares, in a country nine years from independence and not in the mood for him. It receives him as its own and as a problem: a Brahmin clerk's son manufactured by Europeans into a messiah, who has publicly refused the office and now says the same thing to a nationalist audience as to a Theosophical one, that no collective identity, religious or national, will free anybody from anything. The tour runs through 1938.
stops.quote_source: Ninth Talk in Bombay, 14 March 1948; seen via Wikiquote, not a primary transcript
suggested_refs: Transcripts of the Indian talks of 1938, Krishnamurti Foundation India archive

stops.name: Ojai, meeting Aldous Huxley
stops.date_confidence: attested for 1938 in the Ojai region (Wikipedia, 'Jiddu Krishnamurti'; corroborated in general terms by ojaihistory.com). Month and day unknown and defaulted. Huxley's 1954 foreword to The First and Last Freedom is attested.
stops.campa: Aldous Huxley, newly arrived in California, meets him in the Ojai valley. He steers Krishnamurti toward a serious publisher and writes the foreword to The First and Last Freedom in 1954, and that book, more than the twenty years of talks behind it, puts him in front of a reading public that has never heard of the Order of the Star. Huxley is one of the very few people in his life who is neither disciple nor employee. The two of them walk and argue for years about perception, conditioning, war, nationality, and what a mind does when it stops defending itself.
stops.quote: The transformation of the world is brought about by the transformation of oneself.
stops.quote_source: Attributed to The First and Last Freedom (1954), for which Huxley wrote the foreword; seen via Wikiquote, not a primary edition
suggested_refs: Aldous Huxley's foreword to The First and Last Freedom (1954)

stops.name: Ojai, the war years and the Bureau
stops.date_confidence: attested by the KFA timeline, 1935-1944, which records the wartime stay at Ojai, the giving of produce to relief, the FBI's infiltration of his talks under Hoover and the ending of surveillance. The same entry records twice-weekly Oak Grove discussions and twice-weekly Hollywood meetings through 1940-1944, so the common claim that he suspended talks altogether is wrong. Month and day unknown and defaulted.
stops.campa: He cannot travel, and does not try. For four years he stays in the valley, works the land at Arya Vihara and gives the surplus produce to war relief, holding no large public talks but keeping twice-weekly discussions at Ojai and twice-weekly meetings in Hollywood. He has said in public that the war is the outcome of the way people are trained to think, which in 1940 is heard as sedition. Hoover's agents sit in on the meetings, take notes, and follow him on his walks. The surveillance is dropped when the Bureau decides he is no threat.
stops.quote: The individual is the little conditioned, miserable, frustrated entity, satisfied with his little gods and his little traditions.
stops.quote_source: Attributed to Freedom from the Known (1969); seen via Wikiquote, not a primary edition
suggested_refs: The FBI file opened on Krishnamurti during the war years

stops.name: Ojai, the talks resumed
stops.date_confidence: attested for May 1944 (Wikipedia, 'Jiddu Krishnamurti'); day unknown and defaulted. The founding of Krishnamurti Writings, Inc. in 1944 is reconstruction from a single secondary source.
stops.campa: In May he speaks publicly again, in the Oak Grove, after four years without a crowd in front of him. The audience has changed. The Theosophists who came for a World Teacher have largely gone, the war has emptied Europe of its camps and lodges, and what assembles under the oaks is an American public with no organizational reason to be there. The talks are recorded and printed. Krishnamurti Writings, Inc. is founded the same year to hold and publish them, with Rajagopal running it.
suggested_refs: The 1944 Ojai talks, first postwar series in the Oak Grove

stops.name: New Delhi, the return to India
stops.date_confidence: attested for 1947 (Wikipedia, 'Jiddu Krishnamurti'), including the meeting with Nehru, the association with Pupul and Nandini Mehta, and talks at Bombay, Madras, Delhi and Varanasi. Month and day unknown and defaulted.
stops.campa: He returns to an India he has not seen since before the war, in the year of partition, and is received by the new political class: Nehru, who talks with him at length; Pupul and Nandini Mehta, who become lifelong associates and the organizers of his Indian work. What he tells them is what he tells everyone, that nationality is a form of conditioning and that violence proceeds from it. He speaks at Bombay, Madras, Delhi and Varanasi to audiences that include people running a country three months old.
suggested_refs: Pupul Jayakar, Krishnamurti: A Biography (1986)
sources: Krishnamurti Foundation of America archival timelines (thelifeofkrishnamurti.kfa.org)

stops.name: London, David Bohm comes to find him
stops.date_confidence: Bohm's own article dates a first meeting to 1959 and the sustained interaction from 1961, running about a quarter of a century. The location of the first meeting is not confirmed in any source fetched; the coordinate is central London, where Bohm was then teaching, and is an ordering device rather than an attested site. Month and day unknown and defaulted.
stops.campa: David Bohm, an American theoretical physicist then working in London, reads him and seeks him out. Bohm brings a physicist's refusal to be satisfied by a formula, and he is the one man in Krishnamurti's life who is neither student nor staff and argues back from equal ground. They begin to talk, and go on talking for something close to twenty-five years: about thought as a material process, about time, about why a mind that observes itself is altered in the observing.
suggested_refs: The Krishnamurti-Bohm dialogues, recorded and published from 1961 onward

stops.name: Saanen, the tent in the Bernese Oberland
stops.date_confidence: the KFA timeline dates the start of the Saanen talks to 1962, not 1961 as the dossier had it, and records that they continued yearly until 1985. Month and day unknown and defaulted.
stops.campa: The summer talks move to a meadow in the Saanen valley and stay there every year for more than two decades. A tent goes up; people camp in the fields and along the river; there is no membership, no fee for belonging, and nothing whatever to join. They come from every country in Europe and from India and America. He speaks in the mornings and takes questions afterward, for several weeks each summer, until 1985, when he is ninety and ends the series himself.
stops.quote: You cannot depend upon anybody. There is no guide, no teacher, no authority.
stops.quote_source: Attributed to Freedom from the Known (1969); seen via Wikiquote, not a primary edition
suggested_refs: The Saanen Gatherings, 1962-1985, and their recordings in the foundation archives
sources: Krishnamurti Foundation of America archival timelines (thelifeofkrishnamurti.kfa.org)

stops.name: Brockwood Park, the school in Hampshire
stops.date_confidence: the Krishnamurti Foundation Trust was established in the United Kingdom as a registered charity in 1968 and Brockwood Park School opened in 1969 (kfoundation.org; Wikipedia, 'Brockwood Park'). Coordinate corrected to Brockwood Park itself, 51.0339, -1.1086, from the dossier's 51.0736, -1.2394, which lands about 10 km northwest near Cheriton. Month and day unknown and defaulted.
stops.campa: A Georgian house and its grounds in Hampshire become an English school and the European base of the Krishnamurti Foundation Trust, registered the year before as a charity and deliberately outside D. Rajagopal's reach. Brockwood Park takes boarding students from a dozen countries and no religion. In its rooms he records the long conversations with David Bohm that are filmed, transcribed and published: two men in armchairs, working at whether thought can observe itself, for hours at a stretch, with no audience in the room.
stops.quote: The world is me and I am the world.
stops.quote_source: 2nd Seminar Meeting, Brockwood Park, 14 September 1979; seen via Wikiquote, not a primary transcript
suggested_refs: Brockwood Park School and the Krishnamurti Centre, Hampshire

stops.name: Ojai, the suit over his own words
stops.date_confidence: the two sources differ and neither is preferred here: Wikipedia dates the litigation from 1971 with a final settlement in 1986, while the KFA timeline records a complaint filed in the Superior Court in 1972 to recover assets from Krishnamurti Writings, Inc. and a settlement in favour of the foundation in 1974. Month and day unknown and defaulted.
stops.campa: The break with Rajagopal reaches court. Everything he has said since 1929 has been recorded, transcribed and published through an organization Rajagopal controls, and by the seventies Krishnamurti cannot get at his own manuscripts, correspondence and tapes. The man who dissolved an order of seventy-five thousand members now goes to law over who owns his words. Suit is filed in the California Superior Court to recover them. It is settled, reopened, and closed for good in 1986, weeks after his death. He is seventy-six when it starts.
suggested_refs: The California Superior Court file, Krishnamurti Foundation of America v. Krishnamurti Writings, Inc.
sources: Krishnamurti Foundation of America archival timelines (thelifeofkrishnamurti.kfa.org)

stops.name: Arya Vihara, Ojai: three students and two teachers
stops.date_confidence: attested for 1975 at Arya Vihara with three students and two teachers, and for the 1977 move to a 175-acre property on Lomita Avenue in Meiners Oaks (ojaihistory.com; kfa.org). The Meiners Oaks campus geocodes to 34.4418, -119.2811; this stop is pinned at the founding site in the east end of the valley. Month and day unknown and defaulted.
stops.campa: The foundation opens a school at Arya Vihara with two teachers and three students. Arya Vihara is the ranch house he has lived beside since the twenties, and the first classes meet in it. He is eighty, and founding another school, as he has at every place he has stayed longer than a season: Rishi Valley, Rajghat, Brockwood, now the ground he has lived on since 1922. Two years later the school moves across the valley to a hundred and seventy-five acres on Lomita Avenue at Meiners Oaks, and grows.
suggested_refs: Oak Grove School, 220 West Lomita Avenue, Ojai

stops.name: Los Alamos, talking to the physicists
stops.date_confidence: attested for 1984 by ts-adyar.org, which records a visit to Los Alamos National Laboratories to speak with physicists; month and day unknown and defaulted. The content of the exchange is not documented in the sources fetched.
stops.campa: He goes to Los Alamos, to the laboratory where the bomb was designed, and talks with the physicists who work there. The invitation comes out of the years with Bohm, and the audience is professionally committed to the proposition that the world yields to analysis. What he puts to them is what thought is, where it comes from, and whether the instrument doing the analysing has ever been examined by the people using it. He is eighty-nine, and still keeping the annual circuit of India, England, Switzerland and California.
suggested_refs: Recordings of the 1984 Los Alamos discussions in the foundation archives

stops.name: United Nations, New York: the causes of conflict
stops.date_confidence: attested for 1985 under Pacem in Terris Society auspices, with what the foundation describes as a United Nations Peace Medal (KFA archival pages; kfoundation.org). Wikipedia gives 1984-1985 for the UN-related talks. Month and day unknown and defaulted; the substance of the address as summarized here is inference from the foundation's own description of the topic.
stops.campa: At the invitation of the Pacem in Terris Society he addresses the United Nations in New York in its fortieth-anniversary year, ninety years old, on why human beings continue to kill each other after every institution designed to prevent it has been built. What he tells the delegates is that peace cannot be manufactured by an organization, because the division that produces war sits inside each of the people staffing it. They give him a peace medal. He takes it and goes back to Ojai.
suggested_refs: The Pacem in Terris Society address at the United Nations, 1985

stops.name: Vasanta Vihar, Adyar: the last public talk
stops.date_confidence: attested for 4 January 1986 (KFA timeline, 1985-1986; Wikipedia). Pinned at Vasanta Vihar on Greenways Road, the Krishnamurti Foundation India headquarters, which is a separate property from the Theosophical Society estate about 2 km to the south. The foundation's count of more than 5,300 talks since 1910 is its own.
stops.campa: His last public talk is given at Vasanta Vihar in Adyar, a mile or so from the beach where Leadbeater stopped him in the water seventy-seven years earlier. He is very ill and it shows. He speaks anyway, and the foundation's own count puts this at the end of a line of more than five thousand three hundred talks and discussions since 1910. The circuit that opened on that shore closes inside the same square mile of a city he had no particular reason to love. He is ninety years old. He flies out of Madras six days later.
suggested_refs: Vasanta Vihar, Greenways Road, Chennai, headquarters of Krishnamurti Foundation India

stops.name: Ojai, the diagnosis
stops.date_confidence: attested for 10 January 1986: return to Ojai after a difficult flight, tests finding inoperable pancreatic cancer, curative treatment stopped (KFA timeline, 1985-1986; Wikipedia).
stops.campa: He arrives back in California after a flight that nearly finishes him and is taken for tests. The finding is inoperable pancreatic cancer. Treatment meant to cure is stopped, and he is nursed at Pine Cottage by the people around him, going on with what he has always done: seeing visitors, dictating, asking questions of whoever is in the room. He is told he has weeks. The flight out of Madras on the tenth of January turns out to be the last journey he makes. He gives instructions that there is to be no memorial service.
suggested_refs: Mary Zimbalist's record of the final weeks at Pine Cottage

stops.name: Ojai, the last recording
stops.date_confidence: attested for 7 February 1986 (Wikipedia, which reports the statement about an immense energy and intelligence going through the body for seventy years, and that nobody had understood it). The quote carried here comes from a secondary compilation of that tape rather than from a primary transcript or the recording itself.
stops.campa: Ten days before his death he asks for a tape recorder and makes a statement. For seventy years, he says, an immense energy and an immense intelligence has been using this body, and nobody has understood what went through it. He offers no explanation of what he means. He leaves nobody authorized to explain it on his behalf. It is the nearest thing to a claim about himself he has made in public since 1929, and he makes it into a machine, in a bedroom, alone. What he meant by it the record does not say.
stops.quote: If you all knew what you have missed, that vast emptiness.
stops.quote_source: Attributed to the tape-recorded statement of 7 February 1986; seen via a secondary quotations compilation, not a primary transcript
suggested_refs: The tape of 7 February 1986, held in the Krishnamurti Foundation of America archive

stops.name: Pine Cottage, Ojai: death at ten minutes past midnight
stops.date_confidence: attested for 17 February 1986, ten minutes past midnight Pacific Time, at the Pine Cottage and Arya Vihara property in Ojai, of pancreatic cancer, aged 90, with no memorial service held (Wikipedia; KFA timeline, corroborated by ts-adyar.org for date and age). Coordinate corrected to McAndrew Road from the downtown Ojai coordinate carried in the dossier.
stops.campa: He dies ten minutes past midnight at Pine Cottage, in the valley he came to in 1922 with a brother who did not survive it, ninety years old. The pancreatic cancer has taken five weeks from the diagnosis, and he has been nursed through them in the house supporters bought for him sixty-four years earlier. The body is taken away and cremated, without ceremony. The ashes are divided in three and sent to Ojai, to England and to India, so that no single place can become the place. There is no service, no shrine, no tomb and no successor.
suggested_refs: The Krishnamurti Retreat at 1130 McAndrew Road, Ojai, on the property where he died

stops.name: Adyar beach, the ashes into the sea
stops.date_confidence: the division of the ashes among Ojai, England and India, with immersion in the Ganga at Varanasi and at Gangotri and off Adyar beach, is attested by Wikipedia; the specific dispersal dates are not documented and the month here is an ordering device. Coordinate inherited byte-identical from annie_besant.journey.json, which pins the 1909 encounter on this beach.
stops.campa: A portion of the ashes is carried into the sea off Adyar beach, below the compound of the Theosophical Society, where Leadbeater stopped in April 1909 in front of an undernourished boy standing in the water and said he saw an aura without selfishness in him. The rest go into the Ganga at Varanasi and at Gangotri, and into the ground at Ojai and at Brockwood. The Order the Society built around him has been gone for fifty-seven years, and the Society is still at Adyar. Nothing is kept back and no relic is left anywhere to be visited.
suggested_refs: The three dispersal sites: Ojai, Brockwood Park, and the Ganga at Varanasi and Gangotri
